The rusty bicycle still leans behind the house, like a promise no one has the heart to let go. Some days are like that - everything slows down just enough for you to hear yourself think. I started writing this story on an ordinary evening, when the city lights had come on and the traffic outside had thinned.

People say the important things arrive quietly. I never believed that, until I realized how many beautiful moments I had walked past without stopping.

What I didn't notice

Maybe it was the golden light falling across the doorstep at five in the afternoon. Maybe it was my mother's voice calling from the kitchen. Maybe it was the way a stranger smiled at me on the last bus home.

I write all of these down, not to hold on to them at any cost, but to remind myself that life is still kind to me in its own quiet ways.

"Happiness is not a destination, but a way of walking."

And then

This story doesn't really have an ending. It simply stops here, like a photo taken in a hurry. If you've read this far, thank you for staying with me a little longer.

  • Give yourself an afternoon without your phone.
  • Call an old friend.
  • Write down one thing you're grateful for today.

See you in the next story.
